solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Superb examples given by boyfriend with connections

parts.note: a beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend
ties are bonds or connections

explanation.surface: Fine specimens are presented by a well-connected boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely specimens of a kind are called real stunners or beauties, as in 'that car is a beauty'.

clue.text: Striker's great tendency to finish early

parts.note: big means great in size

indicators.note: finishing early means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: A footballer with a big habit of leaving the match early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer but means the famous clock bell at Westminster, which strikes the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bell in London's Westminster clock tower strikes the hours, making it a striker.

clue.text: Former queen with answer starting to lose temper

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned over Britain from 1702 to 1714

indicators.note: starting to points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A past queen whose reply began with her losing her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like anger but here is the verb for toughening metal or glass by heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalworkers toughen glass or steel by heating and slow cooling, which is to temper it.

clue.text: Financial controller right to chase prize

indicators.note: one thing chasing another comes after it, so this letter follows

parts.note: to treasure something is to prize it

explanation.surface: An accountant correctly pursuing an award.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who manages an organisation's funds is its money manager.

clue.text: A sign of commitment to the battle call?

parts.note: an engagement is a battle between armed forces
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A token of loyalty to a summons to war.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal ring worn after agreeing to marry is a token of commitment to a partner.

clue.text: Regret accepting key delivery

indicators.note: one word accepting another takes it inside itself, so these letters go within

parts.note: to rue is to regret
Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone sorry that they accepted a key that was delivered to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery in the sense of being saved or set free from danger is a synonym.

clue.text: Dodge concealed by upping weighted average

indicators.note: upping says the hidden letters are read backwards
concealed by says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Avoiding tax by quietly raising a weighted average figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Dodge concealed' as the definition, but 'concealed by' is the hiding indicator; 'upping' reverses, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or escape it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Vital fault-finder on a line

parts.note: a critic is someone who finds fault

explanation.surface: An important reviewer stands in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial or essential is described as vital, as in a crucial decision.

clue.text: Intellectuals encourage principals

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
heads are principals of schools

explanation.surface: Academics who motivate their head teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever bookish people are informally mocked as boffins or brainboxes, a plural noun like the definition.

clue.text: Profits sketched out, prepares for action

parts.note: a business clears a sum when it makes that as profit

indicators.note: out says the letters of the word are disordered

explanation.surface: Gains are drafted out as the company readies itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors removed clutter from a ship's deck before battle, hence the idiom for getting ready.

clue.text: Herb providing source of nutrition in eggs (scrambled)

indicators.note: scrambled, as eggs are, says the letters before it are jumbled
the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A herb that adds nourishment to a dish of scrambled eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is N (start of 'nutrition') plus IN and EGGS; 'in eggs' looks like a location but 'in' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is a root plant used as a herbal remedy, so it is an example of a herb.

clue.text: In the chair, begging to be executed

indicators.note: an executed person may be beheaded, so the word loses its head letter

parts.note: pleading means begging, as in pleading for mercy

explanation.surface: Someone in the chair is begging not to be put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the chair' suggests the electric chair, but it is the definition: presiding over a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever is in the chair at a meeting presides over it, taking the foremost or principal role.

clue.text: Rampant sex covers in the morning papers

indicators.note: one piece covers another by wrapping round it
rampant means unrestrained or wild, signalling the letters run riot

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for the morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Unrestrained sex is splashed across the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' rearranges SEX into EXS, which covers AM; 'papers' looks like newspapers but means test papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Examination papers are the written tests sat by students, so papers here means tests.

clue.text: Where there's talk on the origin of wine?

definitions.text: Where there's talk on the origin of wine?

parts.words: Where there's talk on the origin of wine
parts.note: the plant that grows wine's fruit is also the informal channel by which rumours are heard

explanation.walkthrough: To hear something 'on the' rumour mill is the idiom; the plant producing wine's fruit gives the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal network carrying gossip is the idiomatic sense; literally it is the climbing plant bearing wine's fruit.

clue.text: Undertook to touch down in paradise

parts.note: to undertake to do something is to promise it
an aircraft touching down is landing

explanation.surface: A pilot vowed to land somewhere heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical land vowed to Abraham's descendants has become a byword for any longed-for heaven on earth.

clue.text: Raised youth — first class student — a master becoming religious leader

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth
A1 means first class, written with the letter I for the figure
L is a learner driver, used for student
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A young prodigy studies hard and grows into a spiritual figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism holds this title, so he is a religious leader.

clue.text: Gathering sorrow, disheartened, and supplying weaponry

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart, the middle letters, is removed leaving the ends

parts.note: arming is supplying weapons

explanation.surface: A mournful crowd losing heart while being armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd gathering in great numbers, like bees, is said to be massing together.

clue.text: Remains loyal to staff, with second purchase rumoured

parts.note: a staff is a walking stick

indicators.note: rumoured means the word is passed on by speech, giving a soundalike

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like BY

explanation.surface: Staff with a second purchase stay faithful, so gossip says.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing by someone through trouble is staying faithful, a phrasal verb in the same tense.

clue.text: Pub lowering heat for a change

indicators.note: doing something for a change means altering it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bar turning down its heating for once.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking place is jokingly called a watering spot, as animals gather to drink at one in the wild.

clue.text: Managed to pinch one and made a transcript

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between, so one word holds the other

parts.note: coped means managed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone managed to steal one document and duplicated it.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing out a duplicate of a text is reproducing it, in the past tense like the definition.

clue.text: The world of Shakespeare is pale pink

definitions.meaning: in The Merry Wives of Windsor Pistol says the world is his for the opening, the source of the saying
a pale greyish-pink shade is named after the shellfish

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare coined the idea of the world as a shellfish to be prised open; the shade is also a colour name.

clue.text: Got back a couple of revolvers (insured)

indicators.note: a couple of letters means the first two from the word that follows

parts.note: an insured item is covered by the policy

explanation.surface: A pair of stolen insured guns was retrieved.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost is to regain or retrieve it, the past tense matching 'got'.

clue.text: Something to regulate flow of visitors initially through valley

indicators.note: one thing going through another sits inside it

parts.note: a vale is a valley

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something controlling the stream of tourists trickling through a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap or stopcock that opens and closes to control liquid or gas is a valve.

clue.text: Sarcasm from press, say, at last

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Sarcastic remarks finally coming from the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press, say' looks like an example of the media; 'say' instead gives its last letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what one means for mocking effect is a close cousin of sarcasm.

clue.text: Hormone that will mostly offend at home

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: to insult someone is to offend them
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A hormone that will usually cause offence when found in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas releases this substance to control blood sugar; it is a well-known hormone.

clue.text: Talk around venue for carnival transport once

indicators.note: around says one word goes round the outside of the other

parts.note: to chat is to talk
Rio de Janeiro is famous for its annual carnival

explanation.surface: Chatter around carnival floats, which were once horse-drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle of the ancient world was a form of transport in former times.

clue.text: Good eyes failed viewer finally, in spring

indicators.note: eyes that failed have gone wrong, so the letters are out of order
finally picks out the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone's good eyesight eventually failed one spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spring that periodically spouts water and steam is a natural geyser.

clue.text: A Brit, for example — one to cast aspersions

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to slander someone is to cast aspersions on their character

explanation.surface: A British person, say, given to badmouthing others.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain is an island nation, so any Brit is an example of someone living on an island.
